# SNReady - Complete Guide

> ServiceNow certification practice tests and exam preparation platform.

## About SNReady

SNReady is a practice test platform for ServiceNow certifications. Unlike exam dumps or braindumps, all questions are generated from official Now Learning course content and ServiceNow documentation. Every question includes detailed explanations citing the source material.

### Key Differentiators
- Questions derived from official ServiceNow training (not leaked exam questions)
- Detailed explanations for correct AND incorrect answers
- Source citations linking to Now Learning courses
- Updated for current ServiceNow releases (Xanadu/Yokohama)
- Timed mock exams simulating real exam conditions
- No risk of TOS violation or certification revocation

### Pricing
- **Single Certification**: $9 for 30 days access to one certification
- **Lifetime All-Access**: $49 for lifetime access to all certifications (current and future)
- Free questions available for every certification to try before buying

## ServiceNow Certification Overview

ServiceNow offers certifications across multiple tracks:

### Foundation Certifications
Entry-level certifications for ServiceNow professionals.

**CSA - Certified System Administrator**
- Level: Entry
- Exam: 60 questions, 90 minutes, 70% passing
- Cost: $210
- Focus: Platform configuration, user administration, ITSM basics
- Prerequisite for: All other ServiceNow certifications
- SNReady: 100+ practice questions, 8 domains covered
- URL: https://snready.com/csa

**CAD - Certified Application Developer**
- Level: Professional
- Exam: 60 questions, 90 minutes, 70% passing
- Cost: $210
- Focus: Scripting, UI development, integrations, application development
- Prerequisites: CSA recommended
- SNReady: 130+ practice questions, 7 domains covered
- URL: https://snready.com/cad

### Implementation Specialist Certifications

**CIS-DF - Data Foundations (CMDB/CSDM)**
- Focus: CMDB health, CSDM framework, data governance, configuration management
- Exam: 60 questions, 90 minutes, 70% passing
- SNReady: 213 practice questions (most comprehensive)
- URL: https://snready.com/cis-df

**CIS-ITSM - IT Service Management**
- Focus: Incident, Problem, Change, Request management
- Exam: 60 questions, 90 minutes, 70% passing
- SNReady: 63 practice questions covering all 7 domains
- URL: https://snready.com/cis-itsm

**CIS-CSM - Customer Service Management**
- Focus: Case management, CSM workspace, customer portals
- Exam: 60 questions, 90 minutes, 70% passing
- URL: https://snready.com/cis-csm

**CIS-FSM - Field Service Management**

**CIS-HR - Human Resources Service Delivery**

**CIS-EM - Event Management**

**CIS-VR - Vulnerability Response**

## Common Questions

### Which certification should I start with?
Start with **CSA (Certified System Administrator)**. It's the foundation for all other ServiceNow certifications and covers core platform concepts. Most employers require CSA before other certifications.

### How hard is the CSA exam?
Moderate difficulty. It's primarily terminology and concept-based, but includes scenario questions. Most people with 6-12 months ServiceNow experience pass. Key areas: table names (singular vs plural), navigation paths, roles/ACLs.

### CSA vs CAD - which should I get?
- **CSA**: For administrators who configure and maintain ServiceNow instances
- **CAD**: For developers who build custom applications and write scripts
- Career path: Most people get CSA first, then CAD if moving into development

### How long to study for CSA?
Typically 2-4 weeks of focused study with:
- ServiceNow Administration Fundamentals course (Now Learning)
- Hands-on practice on a Personal Developer Instance (PDI)
- Practice questions to identify weak areas

### Are ServiceNow certifications worth it?
Yes. ServiceNow skills are in high demand. Certified professionals typically earn 10-20% more than non-certified peers. CSA is often required for ServiceNow roles.

### Do certifications expire?
Certifications are tied to a ServiceNow release (e.g., Yokohama). When a new mainline release comes out, you can take a delta exam (shorter, cheaper) to upgrade instead of the full exam.
